title: Lesson 12 - FlexCard Setup Properties and How They Govern Behavior
description: Recommend the selection of the most efficient data source method for a FlexCard based on performance requirements and data complexity - be able to explain the functionality of the Flexcard setup properties.

questions.question: A FlexCard shows reference data that never changes and is collapsed by default. Which setup configuration is most efficient?
options: Re-fetch on every context change and load the full payload on render
Load once and defer the heavy fetch until the card is expanded
Re-fetch on a short timer so the data stays current
Disable the data source entirely and rely on static JSON
questions.explanation: Static reference data should load once, and a collapsed card should not pay for a heavy payload until it is expanded, so deferring the fetch is the efficient choice. Re-fetching on context change or on a timer adds needless queries for data that never changes. Disabling the source would break the card if it needs any data at all.

questions.question: A card is showing stale data after a user edits the underlying record. What is the most likely cause?
options: The data source query is wrong
The card is not set to re-fetch when the context record changes
The card is expanded by default
The card has no actions configured
questions.explanation: Stale data after a record edit points to the refresh behavior: the card is not re-fetching when the context record changes. A wrong query would show wrong data, not stale data. The expanded state and the presence of actions do not control data freshness.

questions.question: A consultant is auditing a card that fetches far too often and slows the page. Which setup property should they check first?
questions.explanation: Fetch frequency is governed by the load and refresh behavior in the setup properties, so that is the first place to look. Element styling, action wiring, and the title do not control how often the card fetches data.
